title: The email that became two accounts
blurb: No normalization and an auto-verify path.
prompt: One person ended up with two accounts because the draft compared raw email strings, and a third signup was auto-verified after the provider timed out, letting an unowned address login. Signup retries also kept creating accounts. Review it, fix it, and prove uniqueness and deliberate verification.
aiNote: The draft compares raw address strings so case and alias variants become separate identities, and it marks accounts verified when the verification provider times out, converting a provider outage into a way to claim addresses that were never proven owned.
testIdea: Sign up as Alice@x.com then alice@x.com and assert one account; time out the verification provider and assert the account stays unverified and cannot log in; replay a signup and assert the original user id.
followUps: Which normalization rules should a domain control?
How do you handle a phone number recycled by the carrier?
What does the public projection of a user ever need?
